references.text: Joshua is first mentioned as Moses' chosen leader in the battle against Amalek
Joshua is referred to as Moses' servant, showing his close relationship with Moses before he was appointed as successor
Joshua, son of Nun, served as Moses' young assistant in the tent of meeting
God commands Moses to gather seventy elders and promises to take some of the Spirit that is on him and put it on them - a parallel to spiritual equipping for leadership
The Lord took some of the Spirit that was on Moses and put it on the seventy elders - showing God's pattern of equipping leaders with the Spirit
Joshua was filled with the spirit of wisdom because Moses had laid his hands on him - fulfilling the command in Num 27:18
Pharaoh recognizes that God's Spirit is in Joseph - a similar expression about a man having God's Spirit within him
The apostles choose seven men full of the Spirit and wisdom, and lay their hands on them - a New Testament parallel to the appointment of leaders
Paul reminds Timothy to fan into flame the gift he received through the laying on of hands - a New Testament practice reflecting Moses' commissioning of Joshua
The gift in Timothy was given through a prophetic word with the laying on of hands by the council of elders - continuing the biblical tradition for appointment
